findings.title: closeBudget's nil-ActiveWave branch is unreachable and untested
findings.detail: closeBudget's `if st.ActiveWave == nil { return b }` guard (lines 121-123) protects against a case its only production caller cannot produce: cmdCloseWave already returns an error at line 66-68 (`if tgt.st.ActiveWave == nil { return fail(...) }`) before landedClose or closeWaveBudgeted ever run, so closeBudget is only ever invoked with a non-nil ActiveWave. Grep confirms closeBudget has exactly two call sites in the repo — internal/cli/cmd_close_wave.go:100 (guarded as above) and internal/cli/close_budget_test.go, whose budgetState() helper always sets a non-nil ActiveWave (lines 291-302), so the branch is also untested. It is harmless (the returned zero Budget floors to deadline.Floor via deadline.Close's own Floor logic, matching the no-real-work case), but it is defensive machinery for a state this wave's code never reaches — premature generalisation rather than something an actual caller needs.
